correctness.rationale: For 1<p<2 and c>0 the beta integral gives v_z∈Lp exactly when 1/q<Re z<1/p, and direct differentiation gives C_p v_z=z^(-1)v_z. For any Lq annihilator, F_g(z) is holomorphic and uniformly bounded on every strict substrip by Hölder, while on Re z=1/2 its logit change of variables is the Fourier transform of an integrable h(t)e^{t/2}, so F_g≡0 forces g=0. For c<Delta/pi choose width pi*c<d<Delta: the strip-to-disk map sends z_n to -(1-u_n)/(1+u_n), u_n=(n+1)^(-pi*c/d), with divergent Blaschke sum. Uniqueness forces dense span. For c>Delta/pi choose Delta<d_prime<pi*c; the zeros satisfy the Blaschke condition in the wider strip. A nonzero bounded product B(z) with these zeros times e^{z²} has Gaussian decay on each vertical line; inversion plus horizontal contour shift gives h(t)=O(e^{-b_-t}) on t<0 and O(e^{-b_+t}) on t>0 for interior b_-<1/q, b_+>1/p. Under g(x(t))=h(t)/(1-x(t)), the exact logistic Lq weight x(t)(1-x(t))^(1-q) gives tail exponents 1-q*b_->0 and q-1-q*b_+<0, so g∈Lq, nonzero and annihilating. Translated h(t-j) supply infinitely many independent annihilators since their transforms are e^{jz}F(z). This proves infinite codimension without asserting the critical equality. Independently recomputed Git tree and checked derivative/logit map, mapping of sample points, sign of dual-tail exponents, and representative p=3/2 power thresholds. Numerical sums are corroboration, not proofs.
residual_risks: Strict regimes only, 1<p<2, complex Lp and one-sided positive logarithmic sample; equality c=Delta/pi excluded.
No formal Lean proof or human expert attestation was claimed; numerical finite checks do not certify infinite completeness.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Ordinary strip Blaschke is a known necessary condition for bounded analytic zeros and supplies the zero-product construction, but a nonzero disk Blaschke product is not automatically an Lq Cesàro annihilator; the submission adds Gaussian damping, inversion on a larger strip and q-integrability. Prior October work covers c<Delta/pi after sigma=1/2, but its arithmetic-coset obstruction does not cover c log(n+1), whose consecutive gaps tend to zero, impossible for any subset of finitely many hZ cosets with fixed h>0. A sufficiently general older weighted exponential theorem could subsume the result; none verified to do so.

value.rationale: The one-parameter imaginary-logarithmic sampling family is a natural subproblem of the explicit infinite-eigenvector-span question posed by Belli et al. Example 6.5. The exact threshold c=Delta/pi distinguishes density from infinite codimension for every strict c, sharpening the already published one-sided sufficient condition and answering the previously unclassified fast-log regime. The necessary inverse-transform construction connects operator invariant subspaces to strip zero sets rather than merely renaming a known parameter or producing a computational special case. It does not claim the critical case, all eigenvalue subsets, or practical numerical approximation rates.
residual_risks: The result is specific to a fixed centered vertical logarithmic family; arbitrary eigenvalue subsets and critical equality remain open.
The proof uses standard Blaschke/Fourier principles; value rests on the nontrivial exact operator-specific threshold and inverse-transform realization, not originality of those standard tools.

limitations: Domain exactly complex Lp(0,1), 1<p<2, c>0 and sample n>=1 with z_n=1/2+i c log(n+1).
No proof or verdict for the critical equality c=Delta/pi, no arbitrary-E characterization or quotient basis.
